summary: Registers a kind of URI that represents a JSON Web Key (JWK) Thumbprint, as defined in RFC 7638. This lets a thumbprint be used, for example, as a key identifier in places that require a URI. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: A key's thumbprint is like a fingerprint. This gives that fingerprint an address-style name so it can be used anywhere a web-style name is needed.

questions: what is a jwk thumbprint uri
how to use a key thumbprint as a uri
what hash does a jwk thumbprint uri use
subtitle: A URN prefix that lets a JWK Thumbprint be used wherever an identifier must be a URI.

tldr.problem: A JWK Thumbprint is a hash of a key, but some places, such as specific JWT claims, require an identifier that is a URI.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the URN prefix urn:ietf:params:oauth:jwk-thumbprint, followed by a hash algorithm identifier and the thumbprint value, each separated by a colon.
tldr.outcome: A key-derived identifier can be written as a URI and told apart from other URI identifiers such as DIDs. SHA-256 support is mandatory.

today: RFC 9278 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2022, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Thumbprint Needs a URI Form
sections.content:
A JWK Thumbprint from RFC 7638 is a URL-safe representation of a hash over a JSON Web Key (JWK, RFC 7517). This RFC defines a URI prefix that says the rest of the URI is such a thumbprint. That lets thumbprints travel in contexts that require URIs, including specific JSON Web Token (RFC 7519) claims.

The motivating case is the SIOPv2 specification, which uses a JWK Thumbprint URI as a subject identifier derived from a public key. Writing it as a thumbprint URI differentiates it from other kinds of URI identifiers, such as Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs).
sections.eli5: Your fingerprint identifies you, but some forms only accept a web-style address. This gives the fingerprint a proper address form with a label saying what it is.

sections.title: The URI Syntax
sections.content:
The prefix is urn:ietf:params:oauth:jwk-thumbprint. To make the hash algorithm explicit, the prefix is followed by a hash algorithm identifier and then the thumbprint value, each separated by a colon.

So the full shape is the prefix, a colon, the hash name, a colon, and the thumbprint. Putting the algorithm in the URI means a reader never has to guess how the thumbprint was computed.
sections.eli5: It is a label with three parts separated by colons: what kind of thing it is, how the fingerprint was made, and the fingerprint itself.

sections.title: Hash Algorithm Identifiers
sections.content:
The hash algorithm identifier MUST be a value from the Hash Name String column of the IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry. A URI whose identifier is not in that registry is not valid, and applications need to detect and handle that error.

For interoperability, the SHA-256 hash algorithm is mandatory to implement (Section 5), so any two implementations have at least one hash in common.
sections.eli5: The fingerprint method has to come from an official list. Everyone must know the most common method on the list, so they can always understand each other.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 7638 also apply. In addition, some cryptographic algorithms have several public keys that correspond to the same private key. RFC 7748 warns that using a public key as an identifier, with knowledge of a shared secret as proof of ownership and without including the public keys in the key derivation, might lead to subtle vulnerabilities.

The same caution applies to JWK Thumbprint URIs used as identifiers. A recommended way to confirm that the URI matches the actual public key in use is to sign a message that contains the correct public key with the private key. That message may also contain the thumbprint URI, although it can be computed directly from the public key.
sections.eli5: Sometimes different-looking keys behave the same. So if someone claims a fingerprint is theirs, ask them to sign something with the matching key to prove it.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The RFC registers one value in the IANA OAuth URI registry established by RFC 6755: the URN urn:ietf:params:oauth:jwk-thumbprint, with common name JWK Thumbprint URI. The change controller is the IESG and the specification document is RFC 9278.
sections.eli5: The new label was written in an official list so nobody else will use it for something different.
